facility_roles.quote: The South Pole Telescope (SPT) is a 10-meter diameter microwave / millimeter / sub-millimeter wavelength telescope located at the NSF Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station

intervals.label: operations
intervals.quote: The SPT has been operating at the South Pole since February 2007.

intervals.label: SPT-SZ survey camera
intervals.note: The 2500 deg^2 SPT-SZ survey "was completed in 2011" (arXiv:1409.0850 abstract). The SPT-SZ camera itself was in use from the start of operations in February 2007.
intervals.quote: From 2008 to 2011, the SPT-SZ receiver carried out a 2500 square-degree survey of the southern sky at high galactic latitude.

intervals.label: SPTpol camera
intervals.note: SPTpol was "deployed on the 10-meter South Pole Telescope in January 2012" (arXiv:1210.4970) and used "from early 2012 to the end of 2016" (arXiv:1910.05748).
intervals.quote: From 2012 through 2016, the SPT was equipped with the polarization-sensitive SPTpol receiver

intervals.label: SPT-3G camera
intervals.note: SPT-3G "was first installed in January 2017" and "achieved first light in January 2017" (arXiv:1809.00033).
intervals.quote: In January 2017, the SPT-3G receiver was installed on the SPT.

quantity.quote: The South Pole Telescope (SPT) is a 10 m diameter, wide-field, offset Gregorian telescope
the three-band (90, 150, 220 GHz), 16,000-detector, polarization-sensitive SPT-3G camera

name: South Pole Telescope
notes: SPT-SZ, SPTpol and SPT-3G are the three receivers of one telescope (LAMBDA and the SPT site describe them so) and are recorded as dated phases of one experiment, not as separate experiments.
No INSPIRE experiment id is recorded: INSPIRE was not contacted by this stream.

physics_goals.quote: The key initial project is a large-area survey at wavelengths of 3, 2 and 1.3 mm, to detect clusters of galaxies via the Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect and to measure the small-scale angular power spectrum of the cosmic microwave background (CMB).
physics_goals.value: Detect galaxy clusters through the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect and measure the small-scale CMB power spectrum.

physics_goals.quote: The polarization sensitivity of SPTpol will enable a detection of the CMB "B-mode" polarization from the detection of the gravitational lensing of the CMB by large scale structure, and a detection or improved upper limit on a primordial signal due to inflationary gravity waves.
physics_goals.value: With polarization-sensitive cameras, detect CMB B modes from gravitational lensing and search for inflationary gravitational waves.

summary.plain: A ten-metre microwave telescope at the South Pole that maps the faint afterglow of the Big Bang and finds galaxy clusters in it. It has carried three cameras since 2007; the current one has about 16,000 detectors.
summary.technical: 10 m telescope at the NSF Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station (Dark Sector) for CMB temperature and polarization, SZ cluster and lensing surveys: SPT-SZ (2008-2011, 2500 deg^2), SPTpol (2012-2016, polarization), SPT-3G (since January 2017; 95/150/220 GHz; ~16,000 detectors). Operating since February 2007.
